annotations.description: With a hand containing Katara (GWU), Hakoda (3W), Earth Kingdom Protectors (W), and Earthen Ally (G), the player needs colored mana early. Floodfarm Verge produces W unconditionally and can produce U once a Plains or Island is controlled. Jasmine Dragon Tea Shop only produces colorless mana freely, with colored mana restricted to Ally spells/abilities. Playing Floodfarm Verge turn 1 would allow casting Earth Kingdom Protectors (W) on turn 2 with any second land, and better sets up the mana base for Katara on turn 3. Jasmine Dragon Tea Shop's colored mana can only be used on Ally spells, which is relevant but less flexible, and its colorless-first sequencing delays the curve. Since the player likely wants to play a W creature on turn 2, Floodfarm Verge is the better turn-1 land.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Jasmine Dragon Tea Shop as the turn-1 land.
annotations.betterLine: Play Floodfarm Verge turn 1 to have unconditional white mana available for Earth Kingdom Protectors or Earthen Ally on turn 2, saving Jasmine Dragon Tea Shop for a later turn.

annotations.description: Hired Claw is a 1/2 that could attack into the opponent's board. The opponent has Earth Kingdom Protectors (summoning sick, can't block) and a tapped Jasmine Dragon Tea Shop. There are no blockers available, so Hired Claw would connect for 1 damage plus trigger its 'whenever you attack with one or more Lizards, deal 1 damage to target opponent' ability for a total of 2 damage. Additionally, dealing damage would enable Hired Claw's +1/+1 counter ability ('{1}{R}: Put a +1/+1 counter on this creature. Activate only if an opponent lost life this turn'), which could be activated this turn with the untapped Mountain. This is a free attack with meaningful upside (2 damage + a 2/3 creature going forward) and no risk.
annotations.actionTaken: Skipped the attack phase with Hired Claw.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Hired Claw for free damage (1 combat + 1 from Lizard trigger = 2 damage), then activate its +1/+1 counter ability with the Mountain to make it a 2/3.

annotations.description: Spending Burst Lightning (a versatile burn spell that can deal 4 when kicked) to kill Earthen Ally, which is currently just a 1/2 with a very expensive activated ability. The opponent's real threats will be cards like Katara or Hakoda, and this burn spell would be much more impactful against those. Earthen Ally is low-impact in the near term.
annotations.actionTaken: Used Burst Lightning to deal 2 damage to Earthen Ally, killing it.
annotations.betterLine: Save Burst Lightning for a higher-value target like Katara (3/3) or Hakoda (3/5). The Earthen Ally poses minimal threat currently and Burst Lightning could be kicked later for 4 damage against a real threat.

annotations.description: Used Warp to cast Nova Hellkite, which exiles it at end of turn, when they had enough mana (5 lands producing {3}{R}{R}) to hardcast it normally. While lethal was available this turn regardless, hardcasting preserves the 4/5 flyer permanently as insurance if something goes wrong.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Nova Hellkite with Warp for {2}{R}, which exiles it at end step
annotations.betterLine: Hardcast Nova Hellkite for {3}{R}{R} using all 5 available lands, keeping the 4/5 flying creature permanently as insurance. Alternatively, simply attack with existing creatures and use Burst Lightning to finish (Hired Claw trigger + Hired Claw damage + Burst Lightning = lethal even if Katara blocks Sunspine Lynx).
